title: Victorian gold rush
summary: Gold finds in 1851 at Clunes and at Buninyong, which opened the Ballarat field, drew diggers from Melbourne and Geelong. A source records 211,734 ounces raised between 1 August and 6 December 1851, and nearly 100,000 arrivals in 1852 that doubled the Victorian population.

as_recorded.value: Thomas Hiscock found gold at Buninyong on 8 August (1851)
211,734 ounces raised between 1 August and 6 December 1851; in 1852 nearly 100,000 people arrived

where.historical_name: Ballarat goldfields (Golden Point on the Yarrowee), Colony of Victoria

importance.justification: Sources describe Ballarat as the richest goldfield in the world within a month and a population that doubled in 1852.

sources.title: The Ballarat gold rush of 1851 (chapter 50, The Story of Australia, Martin Hambleton)

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on the Clunes find (29 June in the Courier; Hambleton says Esmond made it public on 5 July), so the record dates the rush by the Buninyong find of 8 August, on which both agree. The pin is Golden Point; the goldfields also spanned Clunes and Buninyong. The 1852 end year rests on Hambleton only.
